title: VfmEnvelope
description: vardeFM's own messages on the monitor API (wire version 1): the same envelope as the shared messages, with a `type` that starts with `Vfm`. The shared messages are described by `envelope.schema.json`. Times are samples at 48 kHz on the receive clock.

WireTime.description: A time on the 48 kHz receive clock, in samples since the radio started.

t.description: First sample after the sender's leader: the start of the sync symbols.

t_end.description: Just past the burst's last symbol.

level.description: Speed level of the payload; absent if the burst has no codewords.

cw_ok.description: Codewords that decoded and passed their CRC.

snr_db.description: The receiver's in-band SNR per symbol (Es/N0), in dB.

peak_dbfs.description: Peak audio level over the burst, in dBFS.

level.description: Speed level of the payload; absent if the burst has no codewords.

retry.description: Consecutive retry number, 0 for a first attempt.

repeat.description: A digipeater repeat of another station's burst.

VfmBusy.description: The channel turned busy or free.

VfmConstellationFormat.description: Not a message: the `vfm_constellation` key vardeFM adds to the shared `Hello`, describing its constellation frames. Each is a binary frame with the shared 8-byte header (stream `stream`, format `format`, `t_low` the burst's `t` as in its `VfmBurstRx`), then 8 bytes: level, codewords, scale, bits per symbol, points (u16 LE), data carriers, 0; then per point the in-phase and quadrature values (i8, 1.0 = `scale`) and the carrier index (u8). A client skips binary frames whose stream id it does not know.

scale.description: The value of 1.0 in a point.
